title: reading-notes-llm-inference-papers-and-blogs
content:
Quick personal reading notes + scratchpad for inference-related papers, blogs, and conference takeaways. Mostly bullets and TODOs for follow-ups.

Context / goal:
- Collect ideas we might try in the serving runtime (latency wins, memory reductions, cheaper GPU cycles).
- Shortlist techniques for Redwood Optimize recommendations: kv caching heuristics, quantization tradeoffs, batching strategies.

Papers / posts skimmed (high level):
- FlashAttention family: huge perf wins for long sequences by reordering compute + blockwise attention; good for opt/kernel-level improvements. Implementation notes: needs CUDA kernels and careful memory pinning for streaming; check license and upstream maintenance.
- Grouped KV / compressed KV techniques: tradeoff between prefix reuse and memory growth. Notes: implement a per-route small LRU of recent prefixes + size cap; experiment with eviction heuristics (time-based vs access-count).
- GPTQ / post-training quantization blog posts: 4-bit PTQ gives strong savings with moderate degradation on some heads. Practical idea: offer quantized fallback models per-customer; evaluate quality regression on real prompt sets before recommending.
- Batch scheduling papers: dynamic batching with latency SLO awareness (short-window batching + preempt for small requests). For low-latency tier consider small fixed micro-batches + immediate flush on timeout.

Conference takeaways (notes from NeurIPS/MLSys sessions & slides):
- Kernel selection matters more than model structure for 2x wins at certain seq lengths. Add a runtime metric to surface which kernel is used per request for diagnostics.
- Mixed-precision and tensorization: auto-select FP16/FP32 for attention vs FFN based on observed instabilities.

Small experiments to run (prio order):
1) Micro-batching + latency SLO simulation on dev cluster (simulate mixed small/large requests).
2) KV-cache LRU eviction prototype in Python (can simulate memory vs hit-rate).
3) Simple GPTQ 4-bit pipeline on a 3B model: evaluate on our internal eval suite (cost/speed/quality).
4) Instrument runtime to log kernel choice + sequence length distribution per model.

Open questions / unresolved: 
- How aggressive can we be with quantization for customers on Dedicated without breaking compatibility? (policy + opt-out?)
- When to evict cached prefixes that are rarely re-used but hold large KV size? (size cap vs time cap)
- Autoscaling + burst handling: how to gracefully fallback to cheaper model variant w/out latency spike during transition?

Links / bookmarks (for later reading):
- FlashAttention implementation repo (practical kernels) 
- GPTQ blog posts / tuning notes
- Slides from MLSys session on batching strategies

TODO (actionable):
- [ ] Create a simple perf benchmark that runs long-seq FlashAttention vs baseline on p4d. Record per-token latency and memory. (Assign: Daniel)
- [ ] Prototype KV LRU sim and produce a 1-pager with hit-rate curves. (Assign: me)
- [ ] Add kernel-usage logging flag to the dev runtime (low-overhead) and roll to staging. (Assign: infra team)

Notes-to-self: keep these notes informal; move a cleaned-up summary to confluence once we have experimental numbers. If experiments show >20% token-cost reduction, propose a small pilot for Dedicated customers.
